title: Tool Reference: Recording the Least the Customer Must Spend on a Trade-In Registration
content:
Printed on every registration under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes is the smallest price a new piece may carry for its credit to be usable, and that figure is kept in step with the credit the registration actually carries.

The least the customer must spend is fixed only after the registration's entries carry every upward revaluation of the credit that the programme's window still admits. Until the entries carry them, the figure is not yet fixed.

## What the desk does

The desk performs this action itself. The tool `update_upgrade_minimum_spend_70148cfb` is unlocked and then called by the agent; it replaces the figure printed on that registration. Nothing else on the registration moves: the credit available, the status and the dates are left exactly as they were, and afterwards the registration, and the paperwork the customer is shown, carry the new figure.

## Parameters

- `credit_reference` — the reference number of the trade-in registration being corrected, written on the customer's upgrade paperwork as TU- followed by six digits; it is read from the trade-in registration lookup.
- `upgrade_minimum_spend` — the smallest price a new piece may carry for this registration's credit to be spendable against it, in USD to 2 decimal places, a plain positive number with no currency symbol and no thousands separator; the tool stores it rounded to 2 decimal places by half-up arithmetic at the moment of the call.

## What comes back

A one-line confirmation naming the registration reference and the least the customer must spend as it now stands, in USD to 2 decimal places. A string beginning "Error" means nothing was written; any other string means the registration now carries that figure.
